title: The IEG Field Manual

subtitle: Identity and Execution Governance for Autonomous Systems

author: Maurice Witten
thesis: AI can act. Identity and Execution Governance establishes when those actions may become consequential.
thesisSupporting: The public practitioner field manual for governing identity, authority, Protected Actions, Protected Consequences, execution evidence, and failure pathways across autonomous systems.
supportingStatement: The public reference for the discipline beneath BlockSiFr Consequence Intelligence, covering identity, execution authority, Protected Actions, Protected Consequences, and verifiable proof.
categoryExplanation: Authentication establishes identity. Access control determines which systems an identity may reach. Identity and Execution Governance determines which actions may execute, which consequences a human, AI agent, machine identity, software system, or autonomous workflow may cause, under whose authority, under what conditions, and with what proof.
operatingModel: Open doctrine. Practical guidance. Production protection through BlockSiFr.
boundaryStatement: The doctrine is public. Production assessment, integration, Consequence Intelligence, enforcement, evidence operations, and enterprise support are delivered by BlockSiFr.
governingRules: Ordinary activity should remain Runway until the consequence boundary is crossed.
Protected Actions require consequence-aware authority and verifiable proof.
